lesson.menu_title: If the Expansion Happens — Planning Out Loud
lesson.menu_desc: The first conditional, in the meeting where nobody knows yet what the company will decide -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 5 -- If the Expansion Happens
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rosa M. Mitiko Shida | Lesson 5 -- If the Expansion Happens

listenings.text: Rosa, Victor here, from regional planning. I am going to be quick because I am between meetings. If the board approves the second phase next Thursday, we will open two more offices in the first half of next year, and one of them will almost certainly be in Lima. That is not public yet, so please keep it in this call. What I need from you is a number. If we go ahead, how many corporate accounts in your portfolio will need a second contact person? Not a perfect answer. A range. And if you cannot give me the range by Friday, tell me now, because I will have to put something in the file either way.

Right, planning session, and I want to be honest about what we know and what we do not. We know the budget. We do not know the timing, and the timing is what decides everything else. If the approval comes in November, the first office opens in March and we have a comfortable lead time. If it slips to January, the same office opens in June, and June is the worst month in this business to start anything. So here is how we work today. We plan for November, and we build a contingency for January. Nobody leaves this room with a plan that only works if everything goes right. Unless we have a second version, we do not have a plan at all.

items.situation: Your director asks what happens to your workload if the second phase is approved.
tips: If plus present simple, then will plus the base verb
Give one number, not a paragraph

items.situation: A client asks what will change for him if the regional office opens.
tips: Start with what does not change
Nothing changes for you unless we tell you first

items.situation: Somebody proposes a plan with no second version.
tips: Unless is a strong, professional way to push back
Unless we have a contingency, we do not really have a plan

items.situation: Your manager asks whether you can deliver the numbers by Friday.
tips: As long as sets your condition politely
As long as I get the figures on Wednesday, I will send it on Friday

items.situation: The team is worried the deal will fall through.
tips: Name the risk, then the plan
If it falls through, we will go back to the March proposal

items.situation: Somebody asks what you need in order to say yes.
tips: Turn the answer into a clear condition
If you approve the budget this week, I will start on Monday

extra_audio.text: Victor explains that the board will vote on the second phase next Thursday. Rosa asks what will happen to her portfolio if the vote is positive. Victor answers that two more offices will open and that one of them will probably be in Lima. Rosa says she will need to know the timing before she can give a real number. Victor agrees and asks her for a range by Friday, and Rosa promises the range as long as she gets the target figures on Wednesday.
